Disease Outbreak Disrupts Greek Automotive Industry Operations

A sudden outbreak of viral gastroenteritis at several automotive manufacturing and distribution facilities in Greece has led to significant workforce shortages, disrupting the sector’s operations as companies scramble to contain the spread. Cars Motorcycles and Marine Engine Trade and Import Co SA is among the firms experiencing production slowdowns and temporary closures at affected sites.

According to the Hellenic Automotive Manufacturers Association, at least 20% of assembly line workers at key facilities have reported symptoms including fever, vomiting, and diarrhea over the past week. “We are facing unprecedented absenteeism rates,” said Panagiotis Markakis, spokesperson for the association. “The safety of our workers is our top priority, but the operational impact is already being felt.”

Cars Motorcycles and Marine Engine Trade and Import Co SA confirmed that two of its sites in Thessaloniki and near Piraeus have been partially shut down for deep cleaning and contact tracing. “We are working closely with local health authorities to implement comprehensive testing and hygiene measures,” a company representative said, adding that contingency plans are in place to reroute urgent orders but some delivery delays are unavoidable.

Analysts estimate that automotive output in Greece could drop by up to 15% this month if the outbreak is not contained swiftly. Local dealer networks have reported delays in vehicle shipments and spare parts supply, with some expressing concern about inventory shortages if the situation persists.

The Panhellenic Union of Automotive Workers has called for enhanced protective equipment and paid sick leave for all affected employees. “Rapid action is needed to safeguard both the health of workers and the stability of the industry,” said union leader Maria Nikolakopoulou.

As the outbreak continues, companies and industry groups are urging authorities for coordinated support to minimize disruption and protect public health.
